newsitem.title: USA: Continental pilots to seek mediation on labor deal.
newsitem.headline: Continental pilots to seek mediation on labor deal.

text.p: Continental Airlines Inc. and its nearly 6,000 pilots will seek the help of a federal mediator to reach a new labour contract since the two sides remain far from a compromise, the union said Friday.
"We're as far apart as you can get. We were so far apart from the company's offer that we decided it was best to go to mediation," said Leonard Nikolai, president of the pilot's union.
The two sides have reached tentative agreement on seniority, training and other issues, but scant progress has been made wages and benefits, the union said.
The pilots are seeking a wage increase of up to 38 percent and improved benefits. Continental offered a counter-proposal to the pilots this week.
"We would have expected a low-ball proposal on opening day as an opener. But 45 days in to it, they gave us a proposal that was basically an opener," Nikolai said.
The two sides opened contract talks on April 2.

The International Association of Continental Pilots, which reprsents 4,900 pilots at Continental Airlines and 1,000 pilots at the sister, regional carrier Continental Express, said it is does not expect a new contract agreement to be reached before the target date of June 30.

"I don't think it is achievable. We're willing to put in all the resources needed for the negotiation process, but the date of the contract is not as important as getting a contract with quality," Nikolai said.
After the company's annual meeting in Houston Friday, Chairman Gordon Bethune said contract talks with the pilots were going well and that he expected to have a new pact by July 1.
Bethune said bringing in a mediator did not signal problems. Rather, Continental management generally favours using a mediator to keep talks from bogging down, he said.
"We used a mediator from the outset in our (successful) negotiations with flight attendants (last year)," he said.
Labour experts said it was prudent for the two sides to seek mediation instead of getting bogged down in counter-proposals that would only raise frustration levels.

"Mediation gives both parties a nice, friendly atmosphere in which to negotiate without getting into batting comments back and forth in the media," said Joseph Blasi, a professor at Rutgers University's School of Management and Labour Relations.

Lawyers for both sides will meet on Monday to outline the mediation process. Some negotiations could resume in about two weeks, but formal negotiations with a mediator will not begin for another month at least, Nikolai said.
Continental's class A stock rose 37.5 cents to $34.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.
